### Bounded integers

A Lean `Fin n` parameter or result is a `System.Numerics.BigInteger`, the same as `Nat`. For `Library.mirror (value : Fin 10) : Fin 10`, `Mirror(3)` returns `6`. `Mirror(10)` throws `ArgumentException` with the message `arg0 is not below its Fin 10 bound`. A negative value throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`, as it does for `Nat`. The package checks the bound before it calls Lean, so caller data is unchanged and a later valid call still works. `Fin 0` parameters reject every value, and bounds wider than 64 bits are compared exactly. XML documentation remarks on each method and the package README state the bound. Only top-level parameters and results are supported; see the [installed checks](../evidence/native-fin-hosts-20261006.md).

A Lean `Fin n` parameter is a `&BigUint` and a `Fin n` result is a `BigUint`, the same as `Nat`. The package checks the bound before it calls Lean, so caller data is unchanged and a later valid call still works. `Fin 0` parameters reject every value, and bounds wider than 64 bits are compared exactly. ### Bounded integers

A Lean `Fin n` parameter or result uses the `Nat` representation: `list<u32>` little-endian limbs. The WIT text is the same with or without the bound. For `Library.mirror (value : Fin 10) : Fin 10`, calling `mirror` with `[3]` returns `[6]`. Calling it with `[10]` fails the Wasmtime call with an error whose message is `arg0 is not below its Fin 10 bound`, and the result slot is unchanged. The package checks the bound before it calls Lean, so caller data is unchanged and a later valid call still works. `Fin 0` parameters reject every value, and bounds wider than 64 bits are compared exactly. The package README lists each export's bounds. Only top-level parameters and results are supported; see the [installed checks](../evidence/native-fin-hosts-20261006.md).
